caption:
One spin of Venus takes longer than its year.

Venus needs about 243 Earth days to turn once on its axis, but only about 225 Earth days to go around the Sun. It also spins backward compared to Earth, so the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east.

Surface views are computer-simulated from NASA Magellan radar data.
